I would strongly advise others to ask detailed questions, verify every bill, and compare medicine prices before trusting this hospital with their loved ones.

I experienced extremely bad treatment at Somaiya Ayurvihar Hospital, which is a trust hospital. Honestly, even government hospitals have much better behavior compared to this.
After collecting the case paper, we went to the ward for the check-up. The nurse asked us to fill out a form, but her behavior was extremely rude. It is not possible to explain everything properly to the patient alone.
After this, my wife met the doctor, who was also very arrogant and rude. When my wife showed her the reports, the doctor said, “These are old reports, bring new ones.” My wife politely asked the doctor to please check the date, as they were the latest reports. After checking, the doctor had no answer and went silent.
Is this really the level of professionalism expected from doctors at such a reputed hospital?
This entire experience was extremely disappointing. A hospital of this level should focus on basic respect, patient dignity, and proper communication. The staff and doctors seriously need training in behavior and patient handling.

featured_reviews.review_text:
My experience at Sion Hospital, Mumbai, was a mixed one. The biggest challenge was the extremely long waiting time at almost every step. Getting a case paper could take over an hour, blood tests often required standing in queues for hours, and reports sometimes took days. The hospital is heavily overcrowded, and patients frequently have to wait weeks or even months for appointments and procedures.

I underwent treatment for kidney stones and had a DJ stent in place for four months. During this period, I had to make multiple visits to the hospital. There was a time when I was in such severe pain that I was literally crawling on the floor. Once the treatment process starts, completing it can become a long and exhausting journey due to delays and follow-up appointments.

However, I would like to mention that Dr. Jigar from the Urology Department stood out as a dedicated professional. He was straightforward, strict, and focused on his work. My concerns were never with the doctors but with the burdened healthcare system and the overwhelming patient load.

Unfortunately, I developed an infection while the stent was in place and fell sick multiple times during those four months. Eventually, I chose to discontinue my treatment there and seek alternatives.

Sion Hospital provides treatment to a huge number of patients and serves an important role in public healthcare, but the overcrowding and long delays can make the experience very difficult for patients who are already suffering. This review reflects my personal experience.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Saifee Hospital is a Dawoodi Bohra founded multi-speciality hospital at Charni Road, Mumbai, India, overlooking the Arabian Sea. Saifee Hospital is founded by the head of the Dawoodi Bohra faith, Syedna Mohammad Burhanuddin, dedicated the hospital to the memory of his revered father, Syedna Taher Saifuddin.
History:-
Saifee Hospital was established by the Dawoodi Bohras in 1948 with the aim of providing safe, ethical and affordable medical assistance to people of all faiths and socio-economic backgrounds. In 2000, the foundation of a new hospital on the existing premises was laid down by Dr Syedna Mohammed Burhanuddin. Construction commenced in 2001 and the new hospital was commissioned on 4 June 2005 in the presence of the Prime minister of India, Dr. Manmohan Singh. The architecture of the hospital features a combination of classical Arabian (with domes and arches) and contemporary (with glass curtain facades) styles.
Services:-
The hospital has approximately 257 beds, as well as 44 ICU beds, and 9 operating theaters, and conducts over 10,000 surgeries a year.
Saifee Hospital specializes in bariatric surgeries, cardiology, critical care medicine, dentistry, dermatology, gynecology, hepatology, oncology, neurology, nephrology, ophthalmology, neonatology, high dose radioactive therapy units, and Pressurized Intra Peritoneal Aerosol Chemotherapy (PIPAC). The hospital features a highly advanced Robotic Surgical System to facilitate the surgeon in performing complex but minimally invasive surgery.
In the aftermath of the 2011 Mumbai bombings, Saifee Hospital provided free treatment to victims and others affected by the bomb blast.
